title: Upper & Lower Limbs - source-verified practice
scopeNote: Original practice material. Upper-limb course modules are limited to facts traceable to the seven local teacher transcripts and cross-checked against Gray's Anatomy for Students, 3rd edition. The hand/carpal extension and every lower-limb module are explicitly Gray's-only because no corresponding local teacher source was located; their presence does not imply lecturer weighting.

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Upper limb: pectoral-girdle osteology
modules.summary: Clavicle and scapula orientation, attachments, articulations, fractures, and 3D identification.
modules.sourceLocator: Osteology of the upper limb 1.transcript.txt lines 15-124; Gray's 3e printed pp. 702-717 (local PDF pp. 714-729).
keyPoints: Orient clavicle and scapula from reliable landmarks.
Relate fossae, processes, and articulations.
Recognize common clavicular injury anatomy.

retrieval.prompt: A loose clavicle is being sided in the anatomy laboratory. Which feature should face inferiorly in the correctly oriented bone?
A patient falls on an outstretched hand and fractures the clavicle at its most common weak point. Which location is most likely?
retrieval.answer: Junction of the middle and lateral thirds

retrieval.prompt: When a scapula is held in anatomical position, which orientation of the glenoid cavity is correct?

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Upper limb: shoulder and posterior scapular region
modules.summary: Transcript-grounded scapular spaces, suprascapular and axillary distributions, long-head biceps relation, glenohumeral identification, and axillary-lesion signs.
modules.sourceLocator: Osteology of the upper limb 1.transcript.txt lines 70-99; Axilla 1.transcript.txt lines 2-9 and 30-34; Axilla 2.transcript.txt lines 27-29, 83-89, and 165-172; Arm 1.transcript.txt lines 101-107; Gray's 3e printed pp. 705-719 (local PDF pp. 717-731).
keyPoints: Assign posterior scapular-space boundaries.
Match suprascapular and axillary nerves to their muscles.
Recognize the transcript-described deltoid contour change after axillary injury.

retrieval.prompt: Which muscles are supplied by the suprascapular nerve?
Which muscles are supplied by the axillary nerve?
What visible change follows deltoid paralysis after axillary-nerve injury?
retrieval.answer: A flattened shoulder with a more palpable humeral head

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Upper limb: axilla and its contents
modules.summary: Axillary walls, apex, posterior gateways, clavipectoral fascia, artery parts and branches.
modules.sourceLocator: Axilla 1.transcript.txt lines 2-98; Gray's 3e printed pp. 717-738 (local PDF pp. 729-750).
keyPoints: Assign boundaries and walls.
Distinguish triangular and quadrangular spaces.
Relate pectoralis minor to axillary-artery parts.

retrieval.prompt: During a posterior shoulder approach, the surgeon identifies a space bounded by teres minor, teres major, the long head of triceps, and the surgical neck. Which neurovascular pair occupies it?
retrieval.answer: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery

retrieval.prompt: Which vessel passes through the triangular space between teres minor, teres major, and the long head of triceps?
The second part of the axillary artery is defined by which relationship?
retrieval.answer: It lies posterior to pectoralis minor

modules.subject: anatomy
modules.title: Upper limb: brachial plexus
modules.summary: Roots, trunks, divisions, cords, terminal branches, and upper/lower-trunk clinical patterns.
modules.sourceLocator: Axilla 2.transcript.txt lines 7-164; Gray's 3e printed pp. 740-749 (local PDF pp. 752-761).
keyPoints: Construct trunks and cords.
Map terminal nerves to cords.
Distinguish upper- and lower-trunk lesions.

retrieval.prompt: Which anterior rami unite to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus?
After axillary lymph-node surgery, the medial border of the scapula protrudes when the patient pushes against a wall. Which nerve was most likely injured?
The cords of the brachial plexus are named according to their relationship to which structure?
retrieval.answer: Second part of the axillary artery

retrieval.prompt: A lesion of the musculocutaneous nerve in the axilla would most directly weaken which pair of movements?
Which nerve supplies triceps brachii and is therefore essential for forceful elbow extension?
A midshaft humeral fracture injures the neurovascular bundle in the radial groove. Which pair is at risk?
